boundary: This independently authored matrix is checked against DBCode's public package manifest only after the official package is installed locally. Exact vendor manifest content stays outside this repository, and the wrapper does not inspect, modify, repackage, or reverse engineer DBCode implementation code.

feature_groups.evidence: The one-profile smoke opens Connections Home, fingerprints every counted item in DBCode's unchanged New Connection catalogue without storing its labels, and renders the isolated Database Explorer. The rendered proof reviews JSON input, stages only approved non-secret fields as an owner-only CSV, invokes DBCode's unchanged importer, removes temporary data on cancellation and completion, and keeps a hyphen-path DuckDB connection out of the batch for an exact-version read-only preflight.
The one-profile smoke opens a real SQL file through the focused wrapper without executing it. DBCode execution commands and basic editing actions remain available for normal user work.

Official team policy names query explanations under ai.analysis, but the current official feature pages do not identify a distinct UI route. The wrapper therefore records the capability without claiming a reachable or rendered path until the pinned version is checked.

declared_contributions: separate read, DML, DDL, disconnect, copy, and inferred-relationship tools
focused_routes: Generic Code OSS Chat agent tools
feature_groups.evidence: The exact DBCode package declares twelve language-model tools, but Generic Code OSS Chat is intentionally absent from the focused product. The tools therefore have no current focused Copilot route. The separate HTTP MCP server is the planned focused fallback and remains limited until its lifecycle and OAuth gate pass.

The exact package declares DBCode's MCP server definition provider and the focused host keeps that provider unchanged. This proves that automatic editor registration remains reachable. It does not prove the separate HTTP server, an external client, OAuth, or a live tool call.

The HTTP MCP settings page is reachable. Start, Stop, OAuth revoke, and external client use are only declared and do not yet have a focused route or proof against the pinned version. Keep the server off by default and require a separate compatibility gate before claiming HTTP MCP support.

The exact package declares relationship read and write tools, and the wrapper keeps DBCode relationship views. Copilot tool access is unavailable and HTTP MCP remains limited, so an external tool invocation is not yet proved. Relationship writes can change workspace settings and always require an explicit user-directed action.

The wrapper keeps DBCode's account surface and does not override its team AI policy, but account sign-in and team administration are not exercised in default CI. DBCode roles are policy controls, not a security boundary, so the wrapper does not claim rendered or live team-control evidence.
The wrapper opens the host settings editor with an exact DBCode extension filter, removes the editable settings search and generic category tree, and keeps the unrestricted settings shortcut blocked.

focused_routes: DBCode tools > Show Scratch Files in Finder
feature_groups.evidence: The focused menu resolves DBCode's configured local scratch path, creates it when needed, and asks the native host to reveal it in Finder. This avoids the prior DBCode external file-URL failure while leaving the extension unchanged. The filtered settings route exposes DBCode's path, rotation, and deletion controls.
